Title: LCD Reset bug disables Ethernet

Body:
STM32H743i_eval_lcd.c V3.3.1
The eval board does not have a reset line for the LCD device and if the reset function at line 242 is called it will try to use initialize and use PA2 as the reset line which is used by the RMII ethernet for MDIO.  This will prevent the ethernet phy from working correctly.
At the very least this line should be commented out.  Better still would be to remove the line and all code associated with initializing PA2 for use by the LCD which is found between lines 399 and 417.  It would also be good to remove all associated lines in the .h file for the defines used by the code so no one will question the relevance of an LCD reset.

Title: Wrong core

Body:
FreeRTOS examples are using the CM4F port.
<..>/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/portable/RVDS/ARM_CM4F/port.c
Why don't they use the CM7 port?
<..>/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/portable/RVDS/ARM_CM7/r0p1/port.c

Comments:
[HBOSTM - 2023-05-15T15:59:42Z]
Hello @carlo-dev-git ,

There are two options for running FreeRTOS on ARM Cortex-M7 microcontrollers.
The best option depends on the revision of the ARM Cortex-M7 core in use.
If the revision of the ARM Cortex-M7 core is not r0p1 then either option can be used, but it is recommended to use the FreeRTOS ARM Cortex-M4F port located in the /FreeRTOS/Source/portable/IAR/ARM_CM4F directory.

If the revision of the ARM Cortex-M7 core is r0p1 then use the FreeRTOS ARM Cortex-M7 r0p1 port located in the /FreeRTOS/Source/portable/IAR/ARM_CM7/r0p1 directory.

Best Regards,

[HBOSTM - 2023-06-14T16:24:51Z]

Thank you for this contribution.

With regards,
